The short version, in one line:
  Why some emails turn into white-on-white puddles in Gmail, and what this
  newsletter does about it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
IN THIS ISSUE
  * The white-on-white problem, in one paragraph
  * Tables are the quiet workhorse

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE WHITE-ON-WHITE PROBLEM, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

When your phone switches to dark mode, some email apps quietly fix your
colors for you. They might paint the background dark but forget your text
was already a dark color - so your words vanish.

The fix is simple and a little stubborn: put an explicit background color
and an explicit text color on almost every piece of your email. When you
set the colors yourself, the app stops inventing them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
TABLES ARE THE QUIET WORKHORSE

Modern web pages use fancy layout tools that email apps mostly ignore.
That is not nostalgia - it is that the oldest, plainest building block,
the table, is understood by literally every inbox on earth.

So this newsletter's template is built from tables with inline styles: one
wide wrapper, one fixed 600-pixel-wide card, header band, story slots, a
single callout, and the footer. It looks the same in Gmail as it does in
Outlook.

If you ever forward this issue, it survives the trip. That, not
cleverness, is the goal.

Link (Plain-Word Digest test results and the open-source template):
  https://dylanasdale.github.io/

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ONE THING WORTH YOUR TIME

Tonight, switch your phone's mail app to dark mode and re-read this issue.
Notice anything unreadable? That is exactly the failure mode this template
designs against.

Get the template:
  https://dylanasdale.github.io/
